title: How AI Agents Automate Commercial Policy Servicing, From First Call to Finished Work
summary: How AI agents run commercial policy servicing: one front door for calls, emails, and PDFs, specialist agents for endorsements and COIs, and humans on approval.
body_markdown:
**AI policy servicing uses a team of AI agents to take every post-bind request (endorsements, certificates of insurance, renewals, and reinstatements) from whatever channel it arrives on, match it to the right policy, and carry it through to finished work, with a person approving anything outside guidelines or authority.** A Servicing Agent acts as the front door. Specialist agents do the work behind it. The test of a good system is finished work: an endorsement ready for review, or a certificate in the broker's inbox.


This guide explains how that flow works from first call to finished work, where people stay in the loop, and what a brokerage, carrier, or managing general agent (MGA) should look for when it evaluates AI policy servicing tools.


## **Key takeaways**


- **Servicing is a stream of small, constant requests.** Location additions, certificates, limit changes, renewals, and reinstatements arrive by phone, email, broker portal, and PDF, and each one touches the policy system and a document trail.
- **One front door, many specialists.** A Servicing Agent reads the request, confirms the policy, and hands the case, with its documents, to the agent built for that request type.
- **Measure finished work.** Count a request as done when the endorsement is staged for underwriter review or the certificate reaches the broker. A drafted reply still leaves the work with your team.
- **Replace:** **People keep the judgment calls.** Agents prepare a recommendation (for an endorsement: add, refer, hold, or wait) and cite every source. Underwriters and account managers decide anything outside guidelines or authority.
- **Evaluate on completion.** When you compare tools, ask whether the system finishes the task, asks only for what's missing, and logs every step.


## **What is AI policy servicing?**


Policy servicing is everything that happens to a commercial policy between binding and renewal. A broker asks to add a location, raise a limit, name an additional insured, send a certificate of insurance (COI), reinstate a lapsed policy, or renew on updated terms. Each request is small. Each also touches the policy administration system (PAS) or agency management system, the underwriting rules, and a document trail.


**AI policy servicing hands that work to AI agents that read the request, find the policy, gather what's missing, check the work against your rules, and complete the task.** It differs from a chatbot that answers questions, and from a single extraction tool that pulls data from one document. The agents carry a request across systems until it's done, then stop for a person wherever a decision needs judgment.


Requests reach a servicing team through four main channels:


- Phone calls
- Email
- Broker portals
- PDFs and ACORD forms


The same request can arrive through any of them, so the first job is always the same: work out what was asked and which policy it concerns.


## **Why commercial policy servicing is hard to scale**


**Servicing breaks down at the hand-offs.** Someone reads the request, someone else finds the policy, a third person re-keys the details, and the case waits in an inbox between each step. Our CEO saw this from the customer side when FurtherAI needed a COI naming our landlord.[Writing the request took a minute; getting the certificate back took 27 days](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/ai-insurance-servicing-request-fulfillment) .


The data shows the same pattern across the market:


- **Re-keying is the top pain point.** In the[Ivans 2026 Agency-Carrier Connectivity Trends survey](https://www.ivans.com/news/press-releases/2026/agents-are-choosing-carriers-that-automate-submissions-say-findings-in-2026-insurance-agency-carrier-connectivity-trends-survey-report/) of 702 independent agents, **74% named re-keying data into multiple carrier portals as their biggest workflow pain point** , and 76% said digital submission and policy servicing experiences matter more than commission.
- **Costs have moved the wrong way.** McKinsey found that[insurers' operating expenses as a share of revenue have risen 60% in North America since 2005](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/financial-services/our-insights/how-ai-will-reshape-the-economics-of-insurance-a-ceos-guide-to-strategy) , even after technology lifted productivity across claims, servicing, and policy issuance.
- **Service decides retention.** In[J.D. Power's 2025 U.S. Small Commercial Insurance Study](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250819991006/en/More-Small-Businesses-Consider-Dropping-Their-Insurers-J.D.-Power-Finds) , good service was the most common reason customers gave for staying, and only 55% said they "definitely will" renew.
- **The clerical workforce isn't growing.** The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects employment of[insurance claims and policy processing clerks to fall 2% by 2035](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/office-and-administrative-support/financial-clerks.htm) .


Volume is likely to rise, too. As Aman Gour, FurtherAI's co-founder and CEO, put it: "Making a request now takes seconds, but fulfilling it can still take days." When policyholders and brokers use AI to send and chase requests, the teams on the receiving end get more work through the same inbox.


## **How AI agents handle servicing, from first call to finished work**


FurtherAI runs policy servicing as a[multi-agent system](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/furtherai-launches-multi-agent-system-running-the-full-insurance-relay) : one Servicing Agent at the front desk, and specialist agents that do the work. Here's the flow.


1. **Intake from any channel.** The Servicing Agent answers the call, reads the email, or picks up the portal request or form.[Voice and email intake](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/voice-email-intake-insurance-agencies) puts both channels into the same workflow, so a phoned-in request and an emailed one are handled the same way.
2. **Classify and match the policy.** It identifies the request type and confirms the policy before any work starts. If the policy check fails, the case ends with a summary for the broker instead of moving forward.
3. **Hand off to the right specialist.** The case goes to the agent built for that request, with its documents and context attached, so the broker isn't asked twice.
4. **Gather, check, and assemble.** The specialist asks only for what's missing, waits for the reply, reasons over every source, checks its work against your servicing rules, and assembles the right forms.
5. **A person makes the call.** Anything outside guidelines or authority goes to an underwriter or account manager with a recommendation (for a policy change: add, refer, hold, or wait), every reason linked to its source, and, for changes that need rating, the questions to ask before pricing. FurtherAI assigns these decisions to people as[Tasks](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/the-coverage-issue-3) , with notifications by email or Slack, and in our demos the underwriter approves in Microsoft Teams.
6. **Finished work.** Once approved, the change is written to the PAS or agency management system, and premium, installments, and certificates update. Every step is cited and logged.


‍


Each request type ends in a different piece of finished work:


‍


Request type Handled by Finished work Who decides


Policy change (location, limit, additional insured, broker of record) Endorsement Agent Endorsement staged in the PAS, then issued after approval Underwriter, for anything outside guidelines or authority


Certificate of insurance COI Agent Certificate issued and sent to the requester Account manager, where approval is required


Renewal, reinstatement, quoting, and issuing Further specialist agents Renewal or reinstatement prepared, or quote issued Underwriter or account manager


‍


## **A worked example: adding a location**


A broker emails: "Hi, I need to add a location to my client's policy."


1. The Servicing Agent classifies the email as a policy change, finds the policy, and opens a case.
2. The Endorsement Agent asks the broker for the one missing item, an updated statement of values (SOV).
3. When the SOV arrives, the agent reads it row by row against the live policy and flags anything that contradicts the request.
4. It applies your location rules, such as county and backdating limits, and recommends add, refer, hold, or wait.
5. After the underwriter decides, the endorsement is issued and premium, installments, and certificates update.


The broker touches the process twice: one request in, one document reply out. Nobody re-keys anything. For the full walkthrough, including broker of record changes and additional insureds, see our guide to[endorsement processing automation](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/endorsement-processing-automation) .


Reading SOVs is work FurtherAI already does in production on the submission side. A top-10 global carrier using FurtherAI for[complex SOV intake](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/complex-property-sov-intake) brought intake to **under 10 minutes even for SOVs with 50,000+ locations** , with field-level accuracy above 95% at go-live rising to 97% within six months.


## **What should our brokerage look for in AI policy servicing tools?**


**Look for a tool that takes requests from every channel your clients use, confirms the policy before work starts, hands cases between specialist agents without losing context, applies your rules, keeps a person on every judgment call, and produces finished work with a full audit trail.** Adoption is climbing fast: the Big "I"[2026 Agency Universe Study](https://www.iamagazine.com/2026/10/01/evolving-channel-key-findings-from-the-2026-agency-universe-study/) found 46% of agencies now use AI, up from 15% in 2024. Governance lags, though: the Big "I"[2026 Tech Trends Report](https://agencychecklists.com/2026/02/24/act-report-two-thirds-of-independent-agents-plan-to-increase-ai-use-in-2026-80216/) found 55% of agencies have no written AI use policy.


Use this checklist when you compare tools:


1. **Every channel.** Does it handle calls, email, portals, and PDFs, or only one? 86% of agencies in the Agency Universe Study prefer to service customers by phone, so a tool that only reads inboxes leaves those requests to your team.
2. **Policy matching first.** Does it confirm the right policy before work starts, and stop with a clear summary when it can't?
3. **Clean handoffs.** Do specialist agents receive the documents and context, or does staff pass them along?
4. **Asks only for what's missing.** Does it request specific items, then wait and resume when the reply arrives, instead of asking for a full resubmission?
5. **Your rules.** Does it check work against your guidelines, appetite, and authority levels, written your way?
6. **Human decisions.** Can an underwriter or account manager approve, refer, or hold with the reasoning and sources in front of them?
7. **Citations and audit trail.** Is every step sourced and logged? The NAIC's model bulletin on insurers' use of AI,[adopted in 29 jurisdictions as of November 3, 2026](https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/legal-adoption-map-ai-model-bulletin.pdf) , sets[expectations for governance, documentation, testing, and third-party oversight](https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/ai-issue-brief.pdf) , and your carriers will expect the same of tools that touch their policies.
8. **Finished output.** Does the tool produce the completed endorsement or certificate in your system of record, or only a suggestion someone has to act on?
9. **Integration and security.** Does it work with your PAS or agency management system and with Outlook? Does the vendor hold SOC 2 Type II and contractually commit not to train models on your data? Data privacy and compliance risk is the top AI concern among agencies (24%) in the Tech Trends Report.


**Start with the work you already know is manual.** Leavitt Group, one of the largest independent insurance brokerages, began its FurtherAI rollout with[account manager workflows](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/leavitt-group) such as proposal building, policy checking, document comparison, and loss run analysis. Servicing requests follow the same pattern: high volume, repetitive steps, and a person who needs to sign off.

## How to get started


1. **Pick one request type.** Start with the one that costs your team the most re-keying, usually endorsements or certificates.
2. **Write down the rules.** Capture the checks, referral triggers, and approval levels your team applies today.
3. **Connect the channels and the system of record.** Point the Servicing Agent at your service inbox and phone line, and connect your PAS or agency management system.
4. **Back-test, then go live with approval on.** Run the agents on past requests, compare their output with what your team did, and keep approval on every case until you trust the results.

## **Frequently asked questions**


#### What is AI policy servicing?


AI policy servicing uses AI agents to handle the requests that come in after a policy is bound, such as endorsements, certificates of insurance, renewals, and reinstatements. A servicing agent reads the request from any channel, matches it to the policy, and hands it to a specialist agent that completes the task. Underwriters or account managers approve anything outside guidelines or authority, and every step is logged.


#### What should our brokerage look for in AI policy servicing tools?


Look for a tool that takes requests by phone, email, portal, and PDF, confirms the right policy before work starts, and asks only for missing documents. It should apply your rules, let an account manager or underwriter approve with sources in view, and write finished work to your agency management system or PAS. Ask for SOC 2 Type II and a contractual commitment not to train on your data.


#### Which requests can an AI servicing agent handle?


FurtherAI's policy servicing agents cover policy changes such as location additions, additional insureds, and broker of record changes, plus certificates of insurance, renewals, reinstatements, and quoting and issuing. The Servicing Agent routes each request to the specialist built for it. Requests that fall outside your rules, or that need judgment, go to a person with a recommendation and the sources behind it.


#### Does an AI servicing agent replace account managers or underwriters?


No. The agent does the reading, matching, document chasing, and checking, then prepares the case. An underwriter or account manager makes every decision outside guidelines or authority, with a recommendation of add, refer, hold, or wait and each reason linked to its source. Your team spends less time re-keying and more time on the calls and client conversations that need a person.


#### How does the agent know which policy a request is about?


The Servicing Agent reads the call, email, or form, extracts details such as the insured, broker, policy number, and location, and looks up the live policy before any work starts. If it can't confirm a match, or the policy check fails, the case ends with a summary for the broker instead of moving forward, so nobody works on the wrong policy.


#### How do I know why the agent made a recommendation?


Every recommendation comes with its reasons, and each reason links to its source: a line in the call transcript, a row in the SOV, a field in the policy record, or one of your servicing rules. Every step is logged, so a reviewer can trace what the agent read, what it checked, and who approved the outcome. That record also supports audits and AI governance reviews.


#### How do I automate location additions to commercial property policies?


Have the servicing agent capture the request and confirm the policy, then let an endorsement agent request the updated statement of values, read it against the policy, and apply your location rules, such as county or backdating limits. The underwriter gets a recommendation with sources and rating inputs, and the endorsement is issued after approval. Our endorsement processing guide walks through it step by step.


#### Where should we start with AI policy servicing?


Start with one high-volume request type, usually endorsements or certificates of insurance. Write down the rules your team applies today, connect your service inbox and system of record, and back-test the agents on past requests before going live. Keep approval on every case at first, and relax it only where your authority rules allow.
